newsitem.title: USA: SPS Transaction to defer some revenues.
newsitem.headline: SPS Transaction to defer some revenues.

text.p: SPS Transaction Services Inc said Wednesday it expects to defer to future quarters about $6.0 million to $9.0 million in merchant discount revenues from the fourth quarter.
The deferral relates to changes in client marketing strategies, including promotional payment plans offered by some retailers that offer private label credit cards.

SPS issues private label credit cards and normally receives a percentage of the customer transactions as a fee. But promotional payment plans -- such as extended terms on payment -- could delay those revenues, a spokeswoman said.

SPS also said it has decided to reduce its estimate of loan loss allowances required for loans intended to be securitized, as outlined in previous Securities and Exchange Commission filings. Any benefit from this change, however, will be more than offset by an anticipated increase in the loan loss allowance rate, it added.
SPS also said that, as in any year, the fourth quarter will be impacted by the strength of clients' holiday sales.
Earlier, SPS reported third quarter earnings of $0.21 a share, down from $0.43 a year ago.

"Net income continued to be adversely impacted by an industry-wide deterioration in consumer credit quality and the mix and pricing of promotional payment plans offered to our private label credit cardholders," Robert Wieseneck, president, said in a statement. "We have taken aggressive corrective measures to help mitigate the effects of the negative factors. These actions include tightening credit policies, changing cardholder terms and increasing pricing."

SPS said electronic point-of-sale transactions processed rose 15 percent to 110.1 million compared with 95.4 million during the third quarter last year. The company's active commercial accounts increased 18 percent at September 30 to 764,000 from 647,000 a year ago.

The company ended the quarter with 3.3 million active consumer private label accounts, both owned and managed, a five percent increase over last year. Credit card loans outstanding, including securitized loans, at September 30 were $2.0 billion compared with $1.9 billion a year ago.
